Regions (divisions) of every Bangladesh survey

Source: R/data.R
bdhs_regions.Rd

A crosswalk of the region variable of each survey: one row per survey and region code, with the division it denotes, the stable geographic unit, the DHS API region id, the corresponding boundaries and two trend-consistent groupings.

Usage

bdhs_regions

Format

A tibble with 86 rows and 14 columns:

survey_id

DHS survey identifier (all 13 surveys).

region_var

Region variable of the survey's files: "v024" for the DHS rounds (hv024 in household and household-member files, mv024 in men's files, with the same codes); "codiv" (1999-2000 SPA), "qhregion" (2001 BMMS) and "region" (2014 and 2017 SPA) as given by the DHS Spatial Data Repository.

region_code

Code of the region in region_var.

region_label

Value label of the code as written in the survey file (e.g. "barisal", "rajshani") where the file was checked (label_source == "microdata"), otherwise the region name given by the DHS Spatial Data Repository.

division

Division, canonical lower-case 2022 spelling: one of "barishal", "chattogram", "dhaka", "khulna", "mymensingh", "rajshahi", "rangpur", "sylhet".

division_label

division in title case, e.g. "Chattogram".

includes

Later division contained in this region, if any: "Sylhet" (Chattogram in 1993-94), "Rangpur" (Rajshahi up to 2007), "Mymensingh" (Dhaka up to 2014); otherwise NA.

unit_id

Stable 4-digit geographic unit: "0001" Barishal, "0002" Chattogram incl. Sylhet, "0003" Chattogram, "0004" Sylhet, "0005" Dhaka incl. Mymensingh, "0006" Khulna, "0007" Rajshahi incl. Rangpur, "0008" Rangpur, "0009" Rajshahi, "0010" Dhaka, "0011" Mymensingh. Regions with the same unit_id cover the same area in every survey.

reg_id

DHS API region id (region_id in bdhs_indicators); NA for the 1999-2000 and 2014 SPA and the 2001 BMMS.

trend6

6-division trend grouping used by DHS/NIPORT trend tables: Rangpur -> Rajshahi, Mymensingh -> Dhaka (lower case). NA for 1993-94 Chittagong, which includes Sylhet and can only be split with the district variable (sdistr; see bdhs_harmonize()).

trend5

5-division grouping of 1993-94: as trend6, plus Sylhet -> Chattogram. Comparable in every round.

code_verified

TRUE if the code and its label were checked against the value labels of the survey's microdata (1993-94, 1999-2000, 2004, 2007, 2011, 2014, 2017-18 and 2022 DHS); FALSE for codes taken from the DHS Spatial Data Repository only (1996-97 DHS, SPAs, BMMS).

label_source

"microdata" or "sdr": where region_label comes from.

note

Caveats for the row, if any.

Source

Value labels of the survey files (bdhs_value_labels); DHS Spatial Data Repository region attributes (https://spatialdata.dhsprogram.com/home/, accessed 2026-10-26); bdhs harmonization rules. Built by data-raw/05-build-regions.R.

Details

Bangladesh has gained divisions during the survey period: Sylhet (from Chittagong, 1995), Rangpur (from Rajshahi, 2010) and Mymensingh (from Dhaka, 2015). Codes therefore change meaning across rounds (code 5 is Rajshahi up to 2014 and Mymensingh from 2017-18) and older regions contain later divisions (see includes). Use trend6/trend5 to compare rounds.

The region codes of the 2017-18 DHS follow the microdata (1 Barisal, 2 Chittagong, 3 Dhaka, 4 Khulna, 5 Mymensingh, 6 Rajshahi, 7 Rangpur, 8 Sylhet); the DHS Spatial Data Repository codes 5-8 differently for this survey. The 2017 SPA uses the Repository's coding, which has not been checked against SPA microdata.

See also

bdhs_boundaries() for the polygons (same survey_id, region_code, unit_id and reg_id), bdhs_harmonize() for harmonized division variables, bdhs_indicators for official regional estimates.

Examples

# What does code 5 mean in each round?
bdhs_regions[bdhs_regions$region_code == 5,
  c("survey_id", "region_label", "division", "includes")]
#> # A tibble: 13 × 4
#>    survey_id region_label division   includes
#>    <chr>     <chr>        <chr>      <chr>   
#>  1 BD1994DHS rajshani     rajshahi   Rangpur 
#>  2 BD1997DHS rajashahi    rajshahi   Rangpur 
#>  3 BD1999SPA rasjhahi     rajshahi   Rangpur 
#>  4 BD2000DHS rajashahi    rajshahi   Rangpur 
#>  5 BD2001OTH rajshahi     rajshahi   Rangpur 
#>  6 BD2004DHS rajshahi     rajshahi   Rangpur 
#>  7 BD2007DHS rajshahi     rajshahi   Rangpur 
#>  8 BD2011DHS rajshahi     rajshahi   NA      
#>  9 BD2014DHS rajshahi     rajshahi   NA      
#> 10 BD2014SPA rajshahi     rajshahi   NA      
#> 11 BD2017DHS mymensingh   mymensingh NA      
#> 12 BD2017SPA rajshahi     rajshahi   NA      
#> 13 BD2022DHS mymensingh   mymensingh NA      

# Recode a 2017-18 v024 vector to the 6-division trend grouping
r17 <- bdhs_regions[bdhs_regions$survey_id == "BD2017DHS", ]
v024 <- c(1, 5, 7, 8)
r17$trend6[match(v024, r17$region_code)]
#> [1] "barishal" "dhaka"    "rajshahi" "sylhet"
